elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1, Teleglobe USA Inc. may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period ..." This is an unconditional, unilateral election by our party (Teleglobe USA Inc. is the Customer-side Party in this consortium agreement), i.e. a convenience right. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a naming artefact only \u2014 the clause names our party by its corporate name rather than by the alias "Customer" \u2014 and in substance the right is granted to us alone.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties" \u2014 the notice burden on us is 30 days, in writing, and no longer period or additional condition (consent, majority vote, cure) is imposed.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "the other Parties shall refund to Teleglobe USA Inc., pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination." The refund is expressly pro rata, runs from the effective date of termination, and is owed by the counterparties; "amounts prepaid" is at least as broad as prepaid fees in an agreement that levies contributions rather than fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained 18.1 permits a Party to withdraw only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter" on not less than one year's notice, and 18.2 allows mid-term termination only by unanimous written agreement or a 90% Management Committee majority; no counterparty therefore holds a unilateral mid-term convenience exit. The insertion is expressly limited to Teleglobe USA Inc. and grants no reciprocal right, so this element remains already met.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted notice period is thirty (30) days, not 60\u201390 days. This is the preferred, more favourable figure; the fallback numeric window is simply not implemented (nor need it be, since the preferred level is complete).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: the insertion imposes no early-termination fee, charge, or contingent payment on our withdrawal, so there is nothing to cap. (The retained capital-cost forfeiture sentence is keyed only to "Subparagraph 18.1" and is addressed under the liquidated-damages rule.)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 as retained confines any Party's unilateral withdrawal to "the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; no counterparty may exit for convenience mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice" from a withdrawing Party, which exceeds the 90-day floor.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single insertion supplies the Customer-only convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts, while the pre-existing 18.1/18.2 architecture already denies the counterparties any mid-term convenience exit.

The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" flag reads false only because our party is identified as "Teleglobe USA Inc." rather than by the alias "Customer"; inspected in substance, the operative sentence is an unconditional unilateral Customer election and therefore a convenience right.
Fallback is incomplete (notice is 30 days, outside the 60\u201390 day window), which is immaterial because completion is required at only one level and the preferred level is the more favourable one.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, no reciprocal grant to the counterparties, no survival tail, no expense or damages add-ons, and no procedural machinery beyond the notice and refund the checklist requires. The 25-year commitment, 18.2 mid-term unanimity/90% mechanic, paragraph 23 default remedies, and the capital-cost sentence are all left intact.

Intent is preserved: the insertion opens "Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1", so it overrides only the timing bar in 18.1 and leaves the other Parties' one-year end-of-term exit, the Management Committee process, and all commercial mechanics operative with no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Repair for tidiness, not a checklist failure: give the inserted paragraph an express designation (e.g. "18.1A") in the operative text. The margin comment already calls it "Subparagraph 18.1A" while the rendered clause is unnumbered, and an unnumbered paragraph sitting in the 18.1 block invites an argument that the retained sentence "No credit for capital costs will be made to a Party that terminates its participation in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1" attaches to our convenience withdrawal.
